candidates.name: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons

elections.notes: House of Representatives of the Federation of Nigeria, elected before independence in October 1960. The table gives one combined vote figure (610,677, 8.00%) for the Mabolaje Grand Alliance, Igala Union, Igbira Tribal Union, Niger Delta Congress and the AG- and NPC-affiliated independents; it is shown as Others, so those rows have seats but no votes. Independents combines the AG-affiliated (2 seats) and NPC-affiliated (2 seats) independents. The NPC won the most seats although the NCNC and the Action Group received more votes (lead). Shares are of the 7,628,847 votes in the table. The table gives the electorate (9,043,404) but no votes cast, so no turnout. No change column. The article's results by division do not match today's states, so no region winners.

elections.note: Partly boycotted; marked by manipulation and violence

source.name: Wikipedia, citing Nohlen, Krennerich & Thibaut (1999), Elections in Africa

elections.notes: Others: Dynamic Party 42,834, Republican Party 25,831, Socialist Workers and Farmers Party 20,347, Niger Delta Congress 17,798. Polling in some constituencies in the Eastern Region, Lagos and the Mid-Western Region was put off to 18 March 1965 after a boycott in December (lead); the date is the main polling day. The table (African Elections Database, Nohlen et al.) names the NCNC "National Council of Nigerian Citizens". The NPC-led Nigerian National Alliance held 198 seats in all (lead). Changes marked "New" are null. Shares are of the 5,761,483 votes in the table; no electorate or turnout in the source.

elections.notes: The lead says the elections were held "on 7 July 1979 ... to elect a Senate and House of Representatives on 14 July"; the Senate date is taken as 7 July and the House as 14 July. Shares are of the 12,314,107 valid votes; turnout is the table's (12,532,195 votes cast over 48,633,782 registered). First Senate election, so no change column. Region winners: the party with the most seats in each state, from the article's results-by-state table (Oyediran); only Lagos, Niger and Ogun, the 1979 states whose boundaries match today's (States of Nigeria chronology); the other 16 states were later split.

elections.notes: Shares are of the 16,846,533 votes for candidates (the infobox agrees). The table gives the electorate (48,633,782) but no votes cast, so no turnout. To win outright a candidate also needed 25% of the vote in two-thirds of the 19 states; the Supreme Court upheld Shagari's win (Aftermath section). Region winners: the candidate with the highest share in each state, from the article's by-state table (Oyediran); only Lagos, Niger and Ogun, the 1979 states whose boundaries match today's (States of Nigeria chronology); the other 16 states were later split.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the African Elections Database

elections.notes: The table holds the unofficial results: the count was halted by a court injunction, activists leaked the final figures, and the military government annulled the election on 24 June 1993 (Results section). Shares are of the two candidates' 14,293,396 votes. The article says turnout was "around 35 percent", too rough to use. Region winners: the candidate with the most votes in each state, from the article's table of unofficial results by state; Abia, Enugu, Rivers, Ondo, Bauchi, Plateau and Sokoto are left out because the six states created in 1996 were carved from them (States of Nigeria; Ebonyi State article), and those six did not yet exist.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the African Elections Database

elections.notes: All five parties were affiliated with the military regime and opposition parties were banned; the government annulled the results and fresh elections were held in 1999 (lead). The table gives seats only, with no votes, turnout or chamber size; totalSeats is its total of 282 (the template's own sum). It links the Democratic Party of Nigeria to the Peoples Democratic Party article (a redirect), but that party was founded on 31 August 1998 (its infobox), after this election, so the two are kept apart.

elections.note: Marred by allegations of fraud and vote rigging

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the African Elections Database

elections.notes: Others: 17 other candidates, none with 1% of the vote; the largest was Jim Nwobodo (United Nigeria People's Party) 169,609 (0.43%). The lead says most observers found the conduct relatively peaceful and credible but the elections were "marred by allegations of fraud and vote rigging"; EU observers reported "serious irregularities and fraud" and Buhari challenged the result in court. Shares are of valid votes; turnout is the table's (valid plus 2,538,246 invalid votes over 60,823,022 registered). Region winners: the candidate with the most votes in each state and the FCT, from the article's by-state table.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the Inter-Parliamentary Union

elections.notes: The table (IPU) gives seats only; it also lists Accord with no seats. No change column, votes or turnout. totalSeats (360) is the table's own sum; the article does not state the chamber size. EU observers described the elections as "the worst they had ever seen anywhere in the world" (lead). Region winners: only Bayelsa, Federal Capital Territory, Kwara, Nasarawa, Taraba, the states with their own results article ("2007 Nigerian House of Representatives elections in … State"); the winner is the party that won the most constituencies there; no winner for Federal Capital Territory (tied, or seats without a declared winner could change the lead).

elections.note: Highly controversial; observers reported rampant rigging

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the African Elections Database

elections.notes: Others: 21 other candidates, none with 1% of the vote; the largest was Attahiru Bafarawa (Democratic People's Party) 289,224 (0.82%). The lead calls it "highly controversial"; EU observers described the elections as "the worst they had ever seen anywhere in the world". Shares are of the 35,397,517 votes for candidates (the infobox agrees). INEC released no official turnout; the article's estimate (57.5% of 61.5 million registered) is not used. The results did not include state totals (Results section), so no region winners. The Action Congress is the party later renamed the Action Congress of Nigeria (same article).

elections.notes: Others: 52 other parties, none with a seat or 1% of the vote; the largest was Allied Congress Party of Nigeria 87,233 (0.31%). Region winners: only Bayelsa, Federal Capital Territory, Kwara, Nasarawa, Taraba, the states with their own results article ("2011 Nigerian House of Representatives elections in … State"); the winner is the party that won the most constituencies there.
